messages:
alex_s: Heads-up — Helios Analytics is asking for a performance POC. Goal: sustained 120 QPS, 95th <= 200ms for text-gen (avg prompt ~120 tokens), bursts up to 500 QPS for 2m. They also want a cost estimate for committed vs. hosted tiers. Can ops/infra propose a test plan?

maria_sre: Got it. Primary questions: model size (+quant), seq length distribution, and whether they accept multi-region fallback. Also need to know arrival pattern (poisson vs. steady). Do they require streaming?

alex_s: They'll use non-streaming for now. Prompts mostly 80-150 tokens, responses ~60-120 tokens. Traffic is spiky (thin-tailed bursts at day start). Multi-region fallback ok but they prefer single-region SLA.

jordan_infra: Planning a run: 3 phases — ramp, sustained, burst. Proposal:
1) Ramp 0->150 QPS over 10m
2) Sustained 120 QPS for 30m (collect p50/p95/p99, cpu/gpu util, token/sec)
3) Bursts: 3x 1m bursts to 500 QPS with 5m cooldowns
Use model variants: rwd-small-quant (fp16+8bit), rwd-medium (fp16), fallback rwd-large (fp32) for fallbacks. KV prefix caching enabled.

jordan_infra: k6 script we can run, sample:
```
import http from 'k6/http'
import {sleep} from 'k6'
export default function() {
  http.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', JSON.stringify({model: 'rwd-small-quant', prompt: '<<sample_prompt>>'}), {headers: {'Authorization': 'Bearer $TOKEN'}})
  sleep(0.01)
}
```

lee_product: Add route-level batching window = 15ms for this workload (keeps p95 low). Suggest token cap at 350 for safety. Also enable prefix cache for repeated prompts (Helios has templated prompts).

eva_solutions: For the pricing ask: we can provide a hosted estimate (usage) and a Dedicated commit quote. Quick back-of-envelope: with batching + quant we expect ~30% token cost reduction versus baseline. I can draft a committed-50k-reqs/month SKU vs on-demand comparison. Which metrics do procurement care about?

alex_s: They want both unit token cost and committed minimums + SLA for latency. Also question on encryption: they asked if we can support HSM-backed KMS in private deployments and bring-your-own-key for Dedicated.

maria_sre: Security note: for questionnaire — we need to confirm SOC2 in docs and detail HSM/KMS options. For hosted API we offer managed KMS; for Private/Dedicated we support BYOK via customer KMS or HSM integration (requires infra setup). I'll attach template answers after I vet with security.

deploy-bot: load-test-runner: started run 1738123468 (rwd-small-quant, 120 QPS sustained).

deploy-bot: load-test-runner: phase1 ramp complete, median latency 78ms, p95 169ms, gpu util 64%.

jordan_infra: Nice numbers. Can we add a run with batching window changed to 30ms to see cost/latency tradeoff? Also record token throughput to estimate per-token cost.

deploy-bot: load-test-runner: burst test started (target 500 QPS).

deploy-bot: load-test-runner: burst peak reached 512 QPS, p95 312ms, tail spiked to 720ms on 2 backend nodes — KV cache miss during warmup.

maria_sre: Commentary — burst tail hits due to cold KV cache and backend queueing. Mitigation: pre-warm cache for templates, set graceful fallback policy to rwd-medium for overload windows. Also increase autoscale headroom for Dedicated POC.

alevax: (typo)

eva_solutions: I'll send Helios a short summary + cost delta table and attach the security questionnaire draft. Alex, want me to include the post-burst graph and recommended mitigations?

alex_s: Yes please — include options: 1) commit 50k req/mo + Dedicated reserve for predictable latency, 2) hosted with autoscale + canary fallback. Also note HSM/BYOK path and timeline (approx 4-6 weeks for Private/HSM).

maria_sre: I'll prepare the SOC2 pointer and exact HSM integration steps. Jordan, can you capture the exact k6 run artifacts and raw logs (token counts)?

jordan_infra: Yup — uploading artifacts to the Helios folder and will share link.

alex_s: Great — thanks everyone. I'll set up a short sync with Helios for Monday to walk the plan and pricing. :thumbsup:
